messages:
alex: quick heads-up — our daily sweep flagged a grpcio vuln, CVE-2026-2345, in the model-serving image
sec-bot: NEW: CVE-2026-2345 · https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-2345 · CVSS 8.2 · EPSS 0.72 · public PoC reported (link in ticket)
maya: which image/tag exactly? is it used in prod or only staging?
jamie: infra image `redwood/model-server:stable` pulls `grpcio==1.56.0` via requirements.txt in infra/dockerfiles/model-server\alex: exploit chatter looks real — limited PoC on GH issues but requires crafted request to a poorly validated endpoint. might be exploitable remotely if endpoint exposed
tara: oncall, can you confirm if that endpoint is reachable from internet in any of our clusters? ping owners for dedicated capacity too
oncall: quick network check: model-serving is behind the api-gw in hosted; dedicated clusters may have kube-ingress rules but owners say they don't expose the raw RPC endpoint. running `kubectl get svc -n model` now
infra-sre: confirm we run model-serving in two clusters: hosted-prod (behind gw), dedicated-eu (internal only). no public TCP ports for gRPC discovered
maya: good. still, exploitability not zero — PoC + CVSS 8.2 -> treat as high. propose P1 with 48h patch window, canary rollout 10% then ramp
jamie: suggested remediation: bump `grpcio` to 1.57.2 (security fix), rebuild image, deploy canary 10% for 2h, monitor errors and latency, then 100% if stable. I can own PR and build
alex: agree with plan. also add extra telemetry: enable debug-level gRPC error logs for the canary and add audit log marker for the rollout events
tara: add KMS audit: ensure no new image contains embedded secrets and rotate any keys if we find secret leak during build. sec-bot, please create a ticket and add required checks
sec-bot: Ticket created: INFSEC-2026-457 · assigned to jamie · priority P1
jamie: will open PR now, include dependency-scan, e2e, and quick smoke. scheduling canary at 21:00 UTC to avoid peak traffic
oncall: I'll watch logs & alerts during canary and stand by to rollback if error rate spikes > 3x baseline
maya: decision note: P1/48h -> canary 10% -> 2h check -> full rollout within 4h if stable. owner: jamie. add CVSS and EPSS to ticket metadata
jamie: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/p/12345 · CI started · will squash commits and add CVE references in changelog
sec-bot: CI build passed · container image built · vulnerability re-scan shows grpcio 1.57.2 in new image
alex: nice. maya — can you add a short runbook entry for the canary (what to watch, rollback steps)?
maya: added runbook snippet to INFSEC-2026-457 and linked to ops playbook. include `kubectl rollout undo` and metric thresholds
jamie: canary deployed (10%) at 21:00 UTC. smoke tests running. no errors yet
oncall: monitoring: 0.8x error rate, latency stable. no signs of exploit or new stacktraces
tara: reminder to check KMS access logs for build time around PR merge — look for suspicious GET/Decrypt calls from CI agents
infra-sre: running `trivy` and transitive dependency check for C extensions — grpcio has native wheels, but we validated no new native libs present
jamie: after 2h canary looks clean, ramping to 100% now
sec-bot: Deployment complete · tagged `model-server:stable@sha256:abc123` · INFSEC-2026-457 updated
alex: great work. follow-ups: 1) run full dependency-scan across all images for same vuln 2) add automated alert when high-EPSS CVEs land in pinned deps 3) schedule a short retro if rollout had any issues
maya: I'll take (1) and (2). infra-sre, can you add an automated check in the CI pipeline to fail builds when EPSS>0.5 and CVSS>=7 (configurable)?
infra-sre: yes — will open infra PR with threshold feature flag and let ops opt-in initially
oncall: monitoring all clusters for the next 24h. will escalate immediately if anything looks off
jamie: merged PR, builds are green, patch complete. added CVE note to release changelog
tara: closing action: mark INFSEC ticket as mitigated, but keep open for 30 days to monitor. also add audit-log entry for KMS and deploy actions
alex: thanks team :thumbsup: good catch and quick response
maya: quick reminder — update the vulnerability tracker spreadsheet and tag customers if any dedicated tenants might have been exposed (none found but keep note)
jamie: doing that now, will cc security@redwood.ai if any tenant owners need notification
sec-bot: INFSEC-2026-457 status: mitigated · monitoring window: 30d
alex: closing thread once 24h check passes. great job everyone.
